Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis: Likely acute viral upper respiratory infection with cough and mild dyspnea; clinical picture consistent with a viral syndrome or evolving bronchitis; consideration of early pneumonia given SOB and diabetes/obesity risk; no focal chest findings documented.
- Relevant differentials from DDx (consistent with transcript): 
  - Acute viral upper respiratory infection / influenza-like illness (High likelihood) 
  - Acute bronchitis (Medium likelihood)
  - Early community-acquired pneumonia (Medium likelihood)
  - ACE inhibitor–related cough (Low–Medium likelihood)
  - Allergic rhinitis or post-viral airway reactivity (Low likelihood)
  - Diabetes-related susceptibility to infection (Low–Medium likelihood)
- Working diagnoses supported by transcript and DDx: Acute viral URI/influenza-like illness; possible acute bronchitis; potential early pneumonia considered given SOB and diabetes/obesity risk.
- Plan:
  - Supportive care for presumed viral illness: rest, fluids; consider Paracetamol as needed for feverish symptoms.
  - Antibiotics: discussed as a possibility if symptoms do not improve within 24–48 hours; Amoxicillin prescribed if still not better (oral, frequency stated as three times daily; strength/dose not documented).
  - Return precautions: if symptoms worsen, or if shortness of breath persists/worsens, return or seek urgent care; if not better by next week, re-evaluate.
  - Monitoring: advise patient to monitor temperature and respiratory status; reassess if new/worsening signs occur.
- Health Promotion & Planning:
  - Education on viral illness self-management and hydration.
  - Smoking/vaping cessation support reinforced; vaccination status not addressed here but consider routine immunisations per guidelines (not recorded).
  - Discuss chronic disease management (diabetes and hypertension) and risk reduction; reinforce blood pressure and glycemic control during follow-up.
  - Vaccination considerations (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus) not recorded; consider during future visit.
  - Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA): Not recorded.
  - Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports): Not recorded.
  - Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled: Follow-up in 24–48 hours if not improved; return to clinic if not better by next week.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral upper respiratory infection / influenza-like illness
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Dry cough, rhinorrhea, sore throat, fatigue, feverish/night-sweats, onset within days; features typical of viral illness; SOB can accompany viral syndromes.

- Acute bronchitis (viral or post-viral)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Cough with viral prodrome and mild dyspnea; sore throat and malaise; absence of productive sputum favors viral bronchitis; still plausible in context of recent viral symptoms.

- Early community-acquired pneumonia (bacterial/atypical)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Shortness of breath with feverish symptoms; diabetes/obesity risk; clinician planned antibiotics if not improving; absence of focal lung findings or imaging data leaves pneumonia possible but unconfirmed.
